g.text: codeintel index <repo> · offline, writes only · language detected by extension plurality across `git ls-files`, not a filesystem walk
Index pipeline — every stage completes before the pointer flips
any step fails -> registry status = failed, the previously published index stays live; the semantic stage is the one exception — it may fail without blocking the publish
skips: .gitignore'd files · > 1 MB · generated-file banners · lines > 5000 chars
--semantic-include overrides all three. A table only ever holds one model+revision.
The runtime path never writes: queries open index-<sha>.db read-only and it is never mutated in place. Publishing flips a small `current` pointer via os.replace (POSIX rename(2)),
so a query already reading the old file is never interrupted — there is no downtime window. The package graph is rebuilt, not accumulated: each reindex retracts that repo's own stale edges first.
